sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Objective type questions: two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Traditional media has limited scope for archiving the performance. (ii) Traditional media has an immense variety of forms and themes to suit the communication requirements of the masses.

State true or false: (i) Demonstrations are a useful tool for imparting education through classroom teaching and learning in educational institutions. (ii) Puppetry combines entertainment and education for communicating awareness on social issues.
Match: (a) Demonstration (b) Puppetry with (i) Encourages farmers to try new ideas (ii) Combines entertainment with education.
State true or false: (i) Traditional media is culture-specific. (ii) It needs advanced technology.
Fill in the blanks: Traditional media are most effective in ______, ______ areas and among ______.
State true or false: (i) Electronic media have slow feedback mechanisms. (ii) Traditional media are expensive compared to electronic media.
Fill in the blanks: Integration of traditional media with electronic media should retain the ______ of the traditional form.
Name any two advantages of electronic media.
questions.answer: Wide outreach; messages in no time to many people; recording and archiving (any two).

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Mention any two advantages of traditional media.
questions.answer: They are cost effective and flexible to accommodate new themes; also local, live, with immediate feedback and need no special training.

questions.q: Why do we consider 'flexibility' as one of the important factors of traditional media?
questions.answer: Because their form and content can be changed for the context and new themes, e.g. songs on a social cause or comments on current events in tamasha.

questions.q: What should be done while integrating traditional media with electronic media for development purposes? Write any two points of consideration.
questions.answer: Retain the social authenticity and original form of the traditional media; choose a suitable form for the region; keep collaboration between folk artists and producers.

questions.q: Identify any two uses of traditional media in society. Give suitable examples.
questions.answer: Creating awareness on social issues such as polio immunisation through puppetry, and educating farmers through demonstrations and fairs.

questions.q: List any two disadvantages of electronic media.
questions.answer: They are expensive and less intimate; feedback is slow; special training is required.

questions.q: What are the myths about traditional media?
questions.answer: That they have no relevance in the present context and are not effective for communication.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Traditional Media): attempt A or Module B. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write down any four advantages of traditional media that distinguish them from electronic media. Give examples.
questions.answer: Local and live with direct rapport (street play); flexible to new themes (tamasha); cost effective and need no special training (folk songs); immediate known feedback and emotional appeal.

questions.q: Discuss the relevance of traditional media in modern society.
questions.answer: They reach rural and tribal people and illiterates, are flexible and cheap, preserve culture, give deeper impact through audience participation and are being integrated with electronic media for development messages.

questions.q: Compare traditional media with electronic media.
questions.answer: Traditional media are local, live, intimate, flexible and cost effective but limited in reach and archiving; electronic media reach large heterogeneous audiences instantly with recording but are expensive, less intimate and slow in feedback.
